   398→async function syncHeartRate(
   399→  r2: R2Bucket,
   400→  encoder: Fetcher,
   401→  token: string,
   402→  startDate: string,
   403→  endDate: string
   404→): Promise<number> {
   405→  // Heart rate API uses datetime params and has a 30-day limit
   406→  const data = await fetchAllPages<OuraHeartRate>("/v2/usercollection/heartrate", token, {
   407→    start_datetime: `${startDate}T00:00:00+00:00`,
   408→    end_datetime: `${endDate}T23:59:59+00:00`,
   409→  });
   410→
   411→  if (data.length === 0) return 0;
   412→
   413→  const synced_at = new Date().toISOString();
   414→  const grouped = groupByDay(data, (item) => item.timestamp.split("T")[0]);
   415→
   416→  for (const [day, items] of grouped) {
   417→    const rows: HeartRateRow[] = items.map((item) => ({
   418→      bpm: item.bpm,
   419→      source: item.source,
   420→      timestamp: item.timestamp,
   421→      day,
   422→      synced_at,
   423→    }));
   424→    const parquet = await encodeHeartRate(encoder, rows);
   425→    await writeParquetToR2(r2, "heart_rate", day, parquet);
   426→  }
   427→
   428→  return data.length;
   429→}
   430→
   431→// ============================================
   432→// Main Sync
   433→// ============================================
   434→
   435→export async function runSync(env: Env): Promise<SyncResult> {
   436→  const db = env.DB;
   437→  const r2 = env.DATA_LAKE;
   438→  const encoder = env.PARQUET_ENCODER;
   439→
   440→  // Get valid OAuth token (refreshes if expired)
   441→  let token = await getValidToken(db, env);
   442→
   443→  // Determine date range
   444→  const syncState = await db
   445→    .prepare("SELECT last_sync_at FROM sync_state WHERE id = 'oura'")
   446→    .first<{ last_sync_at: string | null }>();
   447→
   448→  const lastSyncAt = syncState?.last_sync_at ?? null;
   449→  const today = new Date().toISOString().split("T")[0];
   450→
   451→  let startDate: string;
   452→  if (!lastSyncAt) {
   453→    // First sync: use backfill start date
   454→    startDate = env.OURA_BACKFILL_START_DATE || "2024-01-01";
   455→    console.log(`Oura backfill from ${startDate} to ${today}`);
   456→  } else {
   457→    // Incremental: from last sync - 1 day (overlap for idempotent overwrites)
   458→    const start = new Date(lastSyncAt);
   459→    start.setDate(start.getDate() - 1);
   460→    startDate = start.toISOString().split("T")[0];
   461→  }
   462→
   463→  // Split into monthly chunks
   464→  const chunks = splitIntoMonthlyChunks(startDate, today);
   465→  console.log(`Oura sync: ${chunks.length} monthly chunk(s) from ${startDate} to ${today}`);
   466→
   467→  let totalSleep = 0;
   468→  let totalActivity = 0;
   469→  let totalReadiness = 0;
   470→  let totalHeartRate = 0;
   471→  let lastSuccessfulEnd: string | null = null;
   472→
   473→  for (const chunk of chunks) {
   474→    try {
   475→      // Refresh token if needed before each chunk
   476→      token = await getValidToken(db, env);
   477→
   478→      const sleepCount = await syncDailySleep(r2, encoder, token, chunk.start, chunk.end);
   479→      const activityCount = await syncDailyActivity(r2, encoder, token, chunk.start, chunk.end);
   480→      const readinessCount = await syncDailyReadiness(r2, encoder, token, chunk.start, chunk.end);
   481→
   482→      // Heart rate API has 30-day limit; use inclusive day count
   483→      const chunkDays =
   484→        (new Date(chunk.end).getTime() - new Date(chunk.start).getTime()) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24) +
   485→        1;
   486→      const heartRateCount =
   487→        chunkDays > 30 ? 0 : await syncHeartRate(r2, encoder, token, chunk.start, chunk.end);
   488→
   489→      totalSleep += sleepCount;
   490→      totalActivity += activityCount;
   491→      totalReadiness += readinessCount;
   492→      totalHeartRate += heartRateCount;
   493→      lastSuccessfulEnd = chunk.end;
   494→
   495→      console.log(
   496→        `Oura chunk ${chunk.start}~${chunk.end}: ${sleepCount} sleep, ${activityCount} activity, ${readinessCount} readiness, ${heartRateCount} HR`
   497→      );
   498→
   499→      // Rate limit: 1s delay between chunks
   500→      if (chunks.indexOf(chunk) < chunks.length - 1) {
   501→        await sleep(1000);
   502→      }
   503→    } catch (e) {
   504→      const message = e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Unknown error";
   505→      console.error(`Oura chunk ${chunk.start}~${chunk.end} failed: ${message}`);
   506→      if (message.includes("rate limit")) {
   507→        // Skip remaining chunks on rate limit
   508→        break;
   509→      }
   510→      // Other errors: skip this chunk and continue
   511→    }
   512→  }
   513→
   514→  // Only update sync_state if at least one chunk succeeded
   515→  if (lastSuccessfulEnd) {
   516→    await db
   517→      .prepare(
   518→        "UPDATE sync_state SET last_sync_at = ?, updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = 'oura'"
   519→      )
   520→      .bind(lastSuccessfulEnd)
   521→      .run();
   522→  }
   523→
   524→  const total = totalSleep + totalActivity + totalReadiness + totalHeartRate;
   525→
   526→  return {
   527→    service: "oura",
   528→    success: true,
   529→    message: `Synced ${totalSleep} sleep, ${totalActivity} activity, ${totalReadiness} readiness, ${totalHeartRate} heart rate records to R2 Parquet`,
   530→    count: total,
   531→  };
   532→}
   533→
   534→// ============================================
   535→// Routes
   536→// ============================================
   537→
   538→// OAuth2 authorization
   539→app.get("/auth", async (c) => {
   540→  const state = crypto.randomUUID();
   541→
   542→  // Persist state for CSRF validation (expires in 10 minutes)
   543→  const stateExpiry = new Date(Date.now() + 10 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();
   544→  await c.env.DB.prepare(
   545→    `INSERT INTO oauth_tokens (id, access_token, refresh_token, expires_at)
   546→     VALUES ('oura_state', ?, '', ?)
   547→     ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET access_token = excluded.access_token, expires_at = excluded.expires_at`
   548→  )
   549→    .bind(state, stateExpiry)
   550→    .run();
   551→
   552→  const params = new URLSearchParams({
   553→    response_type: "code",
   554→    client_id: c.env.OURA_CLIENT_ID,
   555→    redirect_uri: c.env.OURA_REDIRECT_URI,
   556→    scope: "daily heartrate",
   557→    state,
   558→  });
   559→  return c.redirect(`${OURA_AUTH_URL}?${params.toString()}`);
   560→});
   561→
   562→// OAuth2 callback
   563→app.get("/callback", async (c) => {
   564→  const code = c.req.query("code");
   565→  const state = c.req.query("state");
   566→  if (!code) {
   567→    return c.json({ error: "Missing authorization code" }, 400);
   568→  }
   569→
   570→  // Validate state for CSRF protection
   571→  const storedState = await c.env.DB.prepare(
   572→    "SELECT access_token, expires_at FROM oauth_tokens WHERE id = 'oura_state'"
   573→  ).first<{ access_token: string; expires_at: string }>();
   574→
   575→  await c.env.DB.prepare("DELETE FROM oauth_tokens WHERE id = 'oura_state'").run();
   576→
   577→  if (!storedState || storedState.access_token !== state) {
   578→    return c.json({ error: "Invalid state parameter" }, 400);
   579→  }
   580→  if (new Date(storedState.expires_at) < new Date()) {
   581→    return c.json({ error: "State expired, please retry authorization" }, 400);
   582→  }
   583→
   584→  const res = await fetch(OURA_TOKEN_URL, {
   585→    method: "POST",
   586→    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" },
   587→    body: new URLSearchParams({
   588→      grant_type: "authorization_code",
   589→      code,
   590→      client_id: c.env.OURA_CLIENT_ID,
   591→      client_secret: c.env.OURA_CLIENT_SECRET,
   592→      redirect_uri: c.env.OURA_REDIRECT_URI,
   593→    }),
   594→  });
   595→
   596→  if (!res.ok) {
   597→    const text = await res.text();
   598→    return c.json({ error: "Token exchange failed", detail: text }, 500);
   599→  }
   600→
   601→  const token=[REDACTED] = await res.json();
   602→  const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + token.expires_in * 1000).toISOString();
   603→
   604→  await c.env.DB.prepare(
   605→    `INSERT INTO oauth_tokens (id, access_token, refresh_token, token_type, expires_at, scope, updated_at)
   606→     VALUES ('oura', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, datetime('now'))
   607→     ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET
   608→       access_token = excluded.access_token,
   609→       refresh_token = excluded.refresh_token,
   610→       token_type = excluded.token_type,
   611→       expires_at = excluded.expires_at,
   612→       scope = excluded.scope,
   613→       updated_at = excluded.updated_at`
   614→  )
   615→    .bind(token.access_token, token.refresh_token, token.token_type, expiresAt, token.scope ?? null)
   616→    .run();
   617→
   618→  return c.json({ success: true, message: "Oura connected successfully" });
   619→});
   620→
   621→// Manual sync
   622→app.post("/sync", async (c) => {
   623→  try {
   624→    const result = await runSync(c.env);
   625→    return c.json(result);
   626→  } catch (e) {
   627→    const message = e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Unknown error";
   628→    const status = message.includes("not authenticated") ? 401 : 500;
   629→    return c.json({ service: "oura", success: false, message }, status);
   630→  }
   631→});
   632→
   633→// Stats — list R2 objects count (handles pagination)
   634→app.get("/stats", async (c) => {
   635→  const tables = ["daily_sleep", "daily_activity", "daily_readiness", "heart_rate"];
   636→  const stats: Record<string, number> = {};
   637→
   638→  for (const table of tables) {
   639→    let count = 0;
   640→    let cursor: string | undefined;
   641→    do {
   642→      const list = await c.env.DATA_LAKE.list({ prefix: `oura/${table}/`, cursor });
   643→      count += list.objects.length;
   644→      cursor = list.truncated ? list.cursor : undefined;
   645→    } while (cursor);
   646→    stats[`${table}_files`] = count;
   647→  }
   648→
   649→  const syncState = await c.env.DB.prepare(
   650→    "SELECT last_sync_at FROM sync_state WHERE id = 'oura'"
   651→  ).first<{ last_sync_at: string | null }>();
   652→
   653→  return c.json({ ...stats, last_sync: syncState?.last_sync_at ?? null });
   654→});
   655→
   656→export default app;
   657→

  "new_string": "export async function runSync(\n  env: Env,\n  options?: { startDate?: string; endDate?: string }\n): Promise<SyncResult> {\n  const db = env.DB;\n  const r2 = env.DATA_LAKE;\n  const encoder = env.PARQUET_ENCODER;\n\n  // Get valid OAuth token (refreshes if expired)\n  let token = await getValidToken(db, env);\n\n  const today = new Date().toISOString().split(\"T\")[0];\n  const isManualRange = !!(options?.startDate || options?.endDate);\n\n  // Determine date range\n  let startDate: string;\n  if (options?.startDate) {\n    startDate = options.startDate;\n  } else {\n    const syncState = await db\n      .prepare(\"SELECT last_sync_at FROM sync_state WHERE id = 'oura'\")\n      .first<{ last_sync_at: string | null }>();\n\n    const lastSyncAt = syncState?.last_sync_at ?? null;\n    if (!lastSyncAt) {\n      startDate = env.OURA_BACKFILL_START_DATE || \"2024-01-01\";\n      console.log(`Oura backfill from ${startDate} to ${today}`);\n    } else {\n      const start = new Date(lastSyncAt);\n      start.setDate(start.getDate() - 1);\n      startDate = start.toISOString().split(\"T\")[0];\n    }\n  }"
}

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **dlt (data load tool)** は Python のデータインジェストライブラリで、GitHub の verified source がある
- スキーマ推論、増分ロード（incremental loading）、正規化を自動で行う
- 現在の TypeScript Worker は手動で API ページネーション、Parquet エンコード、R2 書き込みを実装しているが、dlt ならこれらが宣言的に書ける
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

ただし、dlt は Python なので **Cloudflare Workers では動きません**。実行環境をどうするかがポイントです。

**実行環境の選択肢:**

| 環境 | 方法 | メリット | デメリット |
|------|------|---------|-----------|
| **GitHub Actions** | Cron スケジュールで定期実行 | インフラ不要、無料枠あり | 実行時間制限、デバッグしにくい |
| **ローカル / VM** | cron や手動実行 | 柔軟、デバッグ容易 | 常時稼働が必要 |
| **Cloudflare Worker** | sandbox-dbt のように Python を動かす | 統一プラットフォーム | 複雑、依存関係の制約 |

**データの保存先:**
- dlt の `filesystem` destination で **R2 に直接 Parquet を書ける**（S3 互換）
- または DuckDB / Motherduck に書いて transform/core で使う

## Conversation Summary: data-engineering-with-cloudflare Codebase Exploration

### Session Overview
This session continued exploration of the Cloudflare-based data engineering infrastructure, focusing on three specific areas: the sandbox-dbt Worker, the d1-to-iceberg Worker, and confirming dlt usage patterns across the codebase. All three areas have been thoroughly analyzed.

---

### 1. Sandbox-dbt Worker: Python dbt Execution in Cloudflare Workers

**Purpose**: Executes dbt transformations in a containerized Python environment within Cloudflare Workers, triggered via HTTP API or scheduled cron jobs.

**Architecture Overview**:
```
HTTP Request → Hono API → Durable Objects Container → Python dbt Process → R2 Artifacts
                                    ↓
                          Sync State Management
```

**Configuration** (`sandbox-dbt/wrangler.jsonc`):
- **Containerization**: Uses `@cloudflare/sandbox` for Python execution with max 3 concurrent instances
- **Triggers**: 
  - HTTP endpoints: POST /run, GET /runs, GET /runs/:runId
  - Scheduled: Cron at `0 2 * * *` (2 AM UTC daily)
- **Bindings**:
  - R2 bucket "data-lake" → `R2_ARTIFACTS`
  - Durable Objects SQLite migration tag `v1`
  - Environment secrets: R2_ENDPOINT, R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_REPO, GITHUB_TOKEN

**API Interface** (`sandbox-dbt/src/index.ts`):
```typescript
POST /run → RunRequest { ref: string, commands: string[], dbtDir: string }
GET /runs → Lists all executed runs
GET /runs/:runId → Retrieves specific run details
GET /health → Health check
```

**Core Execution Flow** (`dbt-runner.ts`):
1. **Input Validation**: SAFE_REF_PATTERN regex validates git references, prevents path traversal
2. **Git Clone**: Clones specified repository branch/commit
3. **Environment Setup**: Installs Python dependencies using uv package manager
4. **Command Execution**: Runs user-specified commands (typically `dbt run`, `dbt test`)
5. **Artifact Collection**: Gathers outputs from `target/` and `logs/` directories
6. **Parallel Upload**: Stores artifacts in R2 with hierarchical "dbt-runs/" prefix structure

**R2 Storage Pattern** (`r2-artifacts.ts`):
```
dbt-runs/{runId}/targets/manifest.json
dbt-runs/{runId}/logs/dbt.log
dbt-runs/{runId}/target/{model_files}...
```

**Key Architectural Decisions**:
- Containerized approach enables isolated Python execution within 50ms CPU limit by offloading to Durable Objects
- R2 artifact storage enables recovery and audit trails without Workers in-memory constraints
- Parallel Promise.all() for artifact uploads optimizes storage latency
- Git-based code retrieval eliminates need for separate code deployment service

---

### 2. d1-to-iceberg Worker: Oura Health Data Export via Pipelines

**Purpose**: Exports Oura health data from D1 to Cloudflare Pipelines for downstream Iceberg format transformation, using incremental sync with last-export-date tracking.

**Architecture Overview**:
```
D1 Database (Oura Data) → Export Worker → Cloudflare Pipelines → Iceberg/R2
                              ↓
                         sync_state table
```

**Configuration** (`d1-to-iceberg/wrangler.jsonc`):
- **Trigger**: Cron `0 1 * * *` (1 AM UTC = 10 AM JST)
- **Bindings**:
  - D1 database "raw" (id: `30fb49b7-8321-4792-8706-06c9205ce026`)
  - 4 Pipeline destinations: PIPELINE_SLEEP, PIPELINE_ACTIVITY, PIPELINE_READINESS, PIPELINE_HEART_RATE
- **Manual Trigger**: POST /export endpoint for on-demand exports

**Data Model** (`export.ts`):
- **Allowed Tables**: oura_daily_sleep, oura_daily_activity, oura_daily_readiness
- **Heart Rate**: Special handling with cursor-based pagination (PAGE_SIZE = 10000)
- **Sync State**: Tracks `last_sync_at` per data source

**Sync State Management Functions**:
```typescript
async function getLastExportDate(db: D1Database): Promise<string | null> {
  const row = await db.prepare(
    "SELECT last_sync_at FROM sync_state WHERE id = 'oura-export'"
  ).first<{ last_sync_at: string | null }>();
  return row?.last_sync_at ?? null;
}

async function updateLastExportDate(db: D1Database, date: string): Promise<void> {
  await db.prepare(
    "UPDATE sync_state SET last_sync_at = ? WHERE id = 'oura-export'"
  ).bind(date).run();
}
```

**Daily Table Export Logic** (`exportTable()`):
```typescript
// Incremental query pattern
const where = lastExportDate 
  ? `WHERE day > ?` 
  : `WHERE 1=1`;

const query = `
  SELECT *, '${Date.now()}' as loaded_at 
  FROM ${tableName} 
  ${where}
  ORDER BY day DESC
`;

const rows = await db.prepare(query)
  .bind(...(lastExportDate ? [lastExportDate] : []))
  .all<OuraRecord>();

// Send enriched records via pipeline
for (const row of rows) {
  await pipeline.send(row);
}
```

**Heart Rate Export with Pagination** (`exportHeartRate()`):
```typescript
// Composite cursor pattern for multi-record-per-day data
const PAGE_SIZE = 10000;

while (true) {
  const where = 
    cursorDay === null 
      ? `WHERE 1=1`
      : `WHERE (day > ?) OR (day = ? AND timestamp > ?)`;
  
  const query = `
    SELECT *, '${Date.now()}' as loaded_at 
    FROM oura_heart_rate 
    ${where}
    ORDER BY day ASC, timestamp ASC
    LIMIT ${PAGE_SIZE}
  `;
  
  const rows = await db.prepare(query)
    .bind(...(cursorDay !== null ? [cursorDay, cursorDay, cursorTimestamp] : []))
    .all<HeartRateRecord>();
  
  if (rows.length === 0) break;
  
  // Update dual cursor for next pagination
  const lastRow = rows[rows.length - 1];
  cursorDay = lastRow.day;
  cursorTimestamp = lastRow.timestamp;
  
  // Send records via pipeline
  for (const row of rows) {
    await pipeline.send(row);
  }
  
  // Exit if we got fewer records than page size
  if (rows.length < PAGE_SIZE) break;
}
```

**Main Orchestration** (`runExport()`):
```typescript
export async function runExport(env: Env): Promise<string> {
  const lastExportDate = await getLastExportDate(env.DB);
  
  // Parallel execution of 4 data sources
  const [sleepCount, activityCount, readinessCount, heartRateCount] = 
    await Promise.all([
      exportTable(env.DB, env.PIPELINE_SLEEP, "oura_daily_sleep", lastExportDate),
      exportTable(env.DB, env.PIPELINE_ACTIVITY, "oura_daily_activity", lastExportDate),
      exportTable(env.DB, env.PIPELINE_READINESS, "oura_daily_readiness", lastExportDate),
      exportHeartRate(env.DB, env.PIPELINE_HEART_RATE, lastExportDate),
    ]);
  
  const totalExported = sleepCount + activityCount + readinessCount + heartRateCount;
  
  // Only update sync state if data was actually exported
  if (totalExported > 0) {
    await updateLastExportDate(env.DB, new Date().toISOString());
  }
  
  return `Export complete: ${sleepCount} sleep, ${activityCount} activity, ${readinessCount} readiness, ${heartRateCount} heart rate records`;
}
```

**Key Architectural Decisions**:
- **Pipelines Instead of Direct Iceberg Writing**: Uses Cloudflare Pipelines as intermediary, enabling transformation and routing flexibility. Iceberg format writing is a Pipeline destination configuration, not Worker responsibility
- **Incremental Export with Sync State**: Only exports records after `last_sync_at` to minimize data transfer and processing
- **Cursor-Based Pagination for Heart Rate**: Implements composite cursor (day + timestamp) for accurate pagination across multiple heart rate measurements per day without memory overflow
- **Parallel Data Source Export**: Promise.all() executes 4 data sources concurrently, maximizing throughput within CPU time budget
- **Conditional Sync State Update**: Updates `last_sync_at` only if totalExported > 0, preventing false incremental checkpoints on empty exports

---

### 3. dlt (Data Load Tool) Investigation

**Finding**: dlt is **NOT currently used** in the codebase.

**Search Methodology**:
- Regex pattern: `dlt|from dlt|import dlt|dlt-core|dlt\[|\.dlt|dlt\.config`
- Search scope: Entire repository (all file types)
- Result: Zero matches across all files

**Implications**:
- Data ingestion uses direct Worker-based approach (d1-to-iceberg for Oura, likely similar patterns for other sources)
- dlt's declarative pipeline features are not currently leveraged
- All data movement is explicit in Worker code rather than dlt's abstraction layer

---

### 4. Cross-Cutting Architectural Patterns

**Error Handling**:
- Workers trap errors at HTTP endpoint level, returning 500 status codes
- Scheduled jobs log errors to console for Workers Observability monitoring
- No circuit breaker or retry logic in examined Workers (handled at Pipelines/infrastructure level)

**State Management**:
- D1 sync_state table tracks incremental export positions
- Durable Objects handle run state and history for sandbox-dbt
- R2 provides durable artifact storage with timestamped hierarchies

**Security Patterns**:
- Git reference validation with SAFE_REF_PATTERN prevents malicious git operations
- Path traversal protection validates directory names in artifact collection
- Environment secrets (tokens, keys) never appear in code
- Service Bindings enable Worker-to-Worker communication with type safety

**Performance Considerations**:
- 50ms CPU time limit respected through containerized offloading (sandbox-dbt)
- Parallel Promise.all() used for concurrent operations (4 data exports, artifact uploads)
- Pagination (10k records/page) prevents memory exhaustion for high-volume data
- Incremental sync reduces data movement and processing overhead

**Observability**:
- Workers Observability enabled for ingestion Worker (from prior session context)
- Console.log calls surface in Workers dashboard
- R2 artifacts enable audit trails for dbt execution history
- Pipeline monitoring tracks data flow and transformation health

---

### 5. Technology Stack Summary

| Component | Technology | Purpose |
|-----------|-----------|---------|
| **Compute** | Cloudflare Workers + Durable Objects | Serverless edge execution, Python containerization |
| **Data Pipeline** | Cloudflare Pipelines | Data routing, transformation, Iceberg format writing |
| **Storage** | D1 (SQLite), R2 (S3-compatible), KV | Structured data, object storage, cache layer |
| **Code Deployment** | Wrangler CLI, GitHub integration | Worker deployment and scheduling |
| **Package Management** | pnpm (TypeScript), uv (Python) | Dependency management for dual-language stack |
| **Code Quality** | Biome, sqruff | TypeScript/JavaScript and SQL linting |
| **IaC** | Pulumi (Go) | Infrastructure-as-Code for Cloudflare resources |
| **Transformation** | dbt + DuckDB or Databricks | SQL transformation layer (transform/core and transform/fusion) |

---

### 6. File Locations Reference

**sandbox-dbt Worker**:
- `/ingestion/src/services/dbt-runner.ts` - Core execution orchestration
- `/ingestion/src/services/r2-artifacts.ts` - Artifact storage logic
- `/ingestion/wrangler.jsonc` - Configuration with Python container setup

**d1-to-iceberg Worker**:
- `/d1-to-iceberg/src/export.ts` - Data export orchestration (primary file examined in this session)
- `/d1-to-iceberg/src/types.ts` - Env and type definitions
- `/d1-to-iceberg/src/index.ts` - HTTP API and scheduled handler
- `/d1-to-iceberg/wrangler.jsonc` - Configuration with Pipeline bindings

---

### Conclusion

The exploration has revealed a sophisticated Cloudflare-based data infrastructure built on three pillars:

1. **Edge-First Execution**: Workers and Durable Objects enable low-latency processing at Cloudflare's global edge network
2. **Modular Data Movement**: Specialized Workers (sandbox-dbt for transformation, d1-to-iceberg for export) handle distinct pipeline stages
3. **Cost-Optimized Storage**: R2 egress-free costs, D1's integrated SQLite, and incremental sync patterns minimize data movement overhead

The architecture demonstrates mature patterns for serverless data engineering: containerized Python execution, streaming data pipelines, incremental sync with state tracking, and parallel processing within computational constraints. This provides a foundation for scaling data infrastructure across Cloudflare's distributed platform.

### Configure Iceberg Table Format in dlt Resource

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/devel/dlt-ecosystem/destinations/iceberg

Sets the 'iceberg' table format for a dlt resource. This configuration is applied directly within the resource definition using the table_format argument.

```python
@dlt.resource(table_format="iceberg")
def my_iceberg_resource():
    ...
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Iceberg destination in dlt using YAML

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/hub/ecosystem/iceberg

This snippet demonstrates how to configure an Iceberg destination using YAML format in dlt. It includes settings for catalog type, credentials, file system, and capabilities. Sensitive information should be stored in `secrets.toml`.

```yaml
destinations:
  iceberg_lake:
    type: iceberg
    catalog_type: rest
    credentials:
      # we recommend to put sensitive configurations to secrets.toml
      credential: my_polaris_key
      uri: https://account.snowflakecomputing.com/polaris/api/catalog
      warehouse: warehouse
      properties:
        scope: PRINCIPAL_ROLE:ALL
    filesystem:
      # bucket for s3 tables - must match Lakekeeper warehouse if defined
      bucket_url: "s3://warehouse"
    capabilities:
      table_root_layout: "{dataset_name}/{table_name}"
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Iceberg destination in dlt using TOML

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/hub/ecosystem/iceberg

This snippet demonstrates how to configure an Iceberg destination using TOML format in dlt. It includes settings for catalog type, credentials, and file system settings. Sensitive information such as credentials should be stored securely.

```toml
[destination.iceberg]
catalog_type="rest"

[destination.iceberg.credentials]
credential="my_polaris_key"
uri="https://account.snowflakecomputing.com/polaris/api/catalog"
warehouse="warehouse"

[destination.iceberg.credentials.properties]
scope="PRINCIPAL_ROLE:ALL"

[destination.iceberg.filesystem]
bucket_url="s3://warehouse"

[destination.iceberg.capabilities]
table_location_layout="{dataset_name}/{table_name}"
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Iceberg destination in dlt using environment variables

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/hub/ecosystem/iceberg

This snippet demonstrates how to configure an Iceberg destination using environment variables in dlt. It includes settings for catalog type, credentials, and file system. Ensure that the environment variables are set correctly before running dlt.

```bash
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__CATALOG_TYPE=rest
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__CREDENTIALS__CREDENTIAL=my_polaris_key
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__CREDENTIALS__URI=https://account.snowflakecomputing.com/polaris/api/catalog
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__CREDENTIALS__WAREHOUSE=warehouse
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__CREDENTIALS__PROPERTIES__SCOPE=PRINCIPAL_ROLE:ALL
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__FILESYSTEM__BUCKET_URL=s3://warehouse/
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__CAPABILITIES__TABLE_LOCATION_LAYOUT={dataset_name}/{table_name}
```

--------------------------------

### Creating Apache Iceberg Tables with DLTHub on Databricks

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/devel/dlt-ecosystem/destinations/databricks

Illustrates how to create Apache Iceberg tables on Databricks using DLTHub. It specifies the `table_format` as "ICEBERG" and configures Iceberg-specific properties like default write format and compression codec. Delta Lake-specific properties are not compatible with Iceberg tables.

```python
import dlt
from dlt.destinations.adapters import databricks_adapter

@dlt.resource
def customer_data():
    yield from load_customers()  # Your customer data source

# Create an Iceberg table for better schema evolution
databricks_adapter(
    customer_data,
    table_format="ICEBERG",  # Use Apache Iceberg format
    table_properties={
        # Iceberg-specific properties (note: Delta properties are not supported)
        "write.format.default": "parquet",
        "write.parquet.compression-codec": "snappy"
    },
    table_comment="Customer data in Iceberg format for schema evolution"
)
```

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/hub/ecosystem/iceberg

This snippet shows the YAML configuration for an AWS S3 Tables Iceberg REST catalog in dlt. It specifies the catalog type, credentials, and region-specific settings for the S3 Tables REST API.

### Configure Iceberg SQL Catalog in dlt.yml

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/hub/ecosystem/iceberg

Configures the Iceberg destination using a SQL catalog within a dlt.yml file. It specifies the catalog type, connection string for SQLite, and the bucket URL for table storage. Optional AWS credentials can be included for cloud storage.

```yaml
# we recommend to put sensitive parameters to secrets.toml  
destinations:  
  iceberg_lake:  
    type: iceberg  
    catalog_type: sql  
    credentials: "sqlite:///catalog.db"  # connection string for accessing the database  
    filesystem:  
      bucket_url: "path_to_data" # table location  
      # credentials section below is only needed if you're using the cloud storage (not local disk)  
      # we recommend to put sensitive parameters to secrets.toml  
      credentials:  
        aws_access_key_id: "please set me up!" # only if needed  
        aws_secret_access_key: "please set me up!" # only if needed  
    capabilities:  
      # will register tables if found in storage but not found in the catalog (backward compatibility)  
      register_new_tables: True  
      table_location_layout: "{dataset_name}/{table_name}"
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Snowflake Plus Destination in dlt.yml

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/devel/hub/ecosystem/snowflake_plus

Sets up the Snowflake Plus destination in a dltHub project's configuration file (`dlt.yml`). This example shows how to specify the destination type and enable Iceberg table creation with an external volume.

```yaml
destinations:
  snowflake:
    type: snowflake_plus
    external_volume: "<external_volume_name>"
    iceberg_mode: "all"
```

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/devel/hub/ecosystem/iceberg

Iceberg > Configuration​ > Overview​: Currently, the Iceberg destination supports two catalog types:
  * SQL-based catalog. Ideal for local development; stores metadata in SQLite or PostgreSQL
  * REST catalog. Used in production with systems like Lakekeeper or Polaris

--------------------------------

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/devel/hub/ecosystem/iceberg

we recommend to put sensitive configurations to secrets.toml > AWS Iceberg Catalogs​: dlt supports three AWS-backed Iceberg catalogs. Their names correspond to the `catalog_type` value you pass in your destination block:
`catalog_type`| What it talks to under the hood  
---|---  
**`s3tables-rest`**| Uses the AWS S3 Tables Iceberg REST API endpoint, and S3 table buckets  
**`glue-rest`**| Uses the AWS Glue Iceberg REST API endpoint, Lake Formation, and S3 table buckets  
**`glue`**| Uses the AWS Glue Catalog, and normal S3 buckets
```

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
dlt は **Iceberg destination を公式サポート**しています。カタログタイプは以下の2種類:

1. **SQL catalog** (`catalog_type: sql`) — SQLite/PostgreSQL でメタデータ管理。ローカル開発向け
2. **REST catalog** (`catalog_type: rest`) — Lakekeeper/Polaris 等の REST API。本番向け

AWS 向けには `s3tables-rest`、`glue-rest`、`glue` の3つも追加サポート。
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## dlt Iceberg + R2 の実現可能性

**結論: 可能だが、カタログの選択が重要。**

R2 は S3 互換なので `filesystem.bucket_url` に指定できます。問題は **Iceberg カタログをどこに置くか**です。

| カタログ | R2 との相性 | 運用コスト |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| **SQL (SQLite)** | ローカルファイル。Worker 内では永続化できない | 低（ただし永続化の課題） |
| **SQL (PostgreSQL)** | Hyperdrive 経由で外部 PG に接続 | 中（外部 DB 必要） |
| **REST (Lakekeeper)** | セルフホスト or マネージド | 高 |
| **REST (Polaris)** | Snowflake 連携 | 高 |

**現実的な選択肢:**

1. **SQL catalog + SQLite on R2** — カタログ DB を R2 に保存し、実行時にダウンロード→更新→アップロード。シンプルだがカタログ競合リスクあり
2. **SQL catalog + D1/外部 PostgreSQL** — D1 は SQLite なので相性良い。ただし dlt が D1 の HTTP API を直接叩けるかは未検証
3. **REST catalog (Lakekeeper)** — Lakekeeper を別 Worker or 外部でホスト。本格的だが構成が複雑

個人プロジェクトなら **SQLite カタログを R2 に保存する方式**が最もシンプルだと思います。どう思いますか？

## R2 Data Catalog is a managed Apache Iceberg data catalog built directly into R2 buckets

Apr 10, 2025 

[ R2 ](/r2/) 

Today, we're launching [R2 Data Catalog](/r2/data-catalog/) in open beta, a managed Apache Iceberg catalog built directly into your [Cloudflare R2](/r2/) bucket.

If you're not already familiar with it, [Apache Iceberg ↗](https://iceberg.apache.org/) is an open table format designed to handle large-scale analytics datasets stored in object storage, offering ACID transactions and schema evolution. R2 Data Catalog exposes a standard Iceberg REST catalog interface, so you can connect engines like [Spark](/r2/data-catalog/config-examples/spark-scala/), [Snowflake](/r2/data-catalog/config-examples/snowflake/), and [PyIceberg](/r2/data-catalog/config-examples/pyiceberg/) to start querying your tables using the tools you already know.

To enable a data catalog on your R2 bucket, find **R2 Data Catalog** in your buckets settings in the dashboard, or run:

Terminal window

```

npx wrangler r2 bucket catalog enable my-bucket


```

And that's it. You'll get a catalog URI and warehouse you can plug into your favorite Iceberg engines.

Visit our [getting started guide](/r2/data-catalog/get-started/) for step-by-step instructions on enabling R2 Data Catalog, creating tables, and running your first queries.

# R2 Data Catalog

R2 Data Catalog sinks write processed data from pipelines as [Apache Iceberg ↗](https://iceberg.apache.org/) tables to [R2 Data Catalog](/r2/data-catalog/). Iceberg tables provide ACID transactions, schema evolution, and time travel capabilities for analytics workloads.

To create an R2 Data Catalog sink, run the [pipelines sinks create](/workers/wrangler/commands/#pipelines-sinks-create) command and specify the sink type, target bucket, namespace, and table name:

Terminal window

```

npx wrangler pipelines sinks create my-sink \

  --type r2-data-catalog \

  --bucket my-bucket \

  --namespace my_namespace \

  --table my_table \

  --catalog-token YOUR_CATALOG_TOKEN


```

The sink will create the specified namespace and table if they do not exist. Sinks cannot be created for existing Iceberg tables.

## Format

R2 Data Catalog sinks only support Parquet format. JSON format is not supported for Iceberg tables.

### Compression options

Configure Parquet compression for optimal storage and query performance:

Terminal window

```

--compression zstd


```

**Available compression options:**

* `zstd` (default) - Best compression ratio
* `snappy` \- Fastest compression
* `gzip` \- Good compression, widely supported
* `lz4` \- Fast compression with reasonable ratio
* `uncompressed` \- No compression

### Row group size

[Row groups ↗](https://parquet.apache.org/docs/file-format/configurations/) are sets of rows in a Parquet file that are stored together, affecting memory usage and query performance. Configure the target row group size in MB:

# R2 Data Catalog

Note

R2 Data Catalog is in **public beta**, and any developer with an [R2 subscription](/r2/pricing/) can start using it. Currently, outside of standard R2 storage and operations, you will not be billed for your use of R2 Data Catalog.

R2 Data Catalog is a managed [Apache Iceberg ↗](https://iceberg.apache.org/) data catalog built directly into your R2 bucket. It exposes a standard Iceberg REST catalog interface, so you can connect the engines you already use, like [Spark](/r2/data-catalog/config-examples/spark-scala/), [Snowflake](/r2/data-catalog/config-examples/snowflake/), and [PyIceberg](/r2/data-catalog/config-examples/pyiceberg/).

R2 Data Catalog makes it easy to turn an R2 bucket into a data warehouse or lakehouse for a variety of analytical workloads including log analytics, business intelligence, and data pipelines. R2's zero-egress fee model means that data users and consumers can access and analyze data from different clouds, data platforms, or regions without incurring transfer costs.

To get started with R2 Data Catalog, refer to the [R2 Data Catalog: Getting started](/r2/data-catalog/get-started/).

## What is Apache Iceberg?

[Apache Iceberg ↗](https://iceberg.apache.org/) is an open table format designed to handle large-scale analytics datasets stored in object storage. Key features include:

* ACID transactions - Ensures reliable, concurrent reads and writes with full data integrity.
* Optimized metadata - Avoids costly full table scans by using indexed metadata for faster queries.
* Full schema evolution - Allows adding, renaming, and dele
rites with full data integrity.
* Optimized metadata - Avoids costly full table scans by using indexed metadata for faster queries.
* Full schema evolution - Allows adding, renaming, and deleting columns without rewriting data.

Iceberg is already [widely supported ↗](https://iceberg.apache.org/vendors/) by engines like Apache Spark, Trino, Snowflake, DuckDB, and ClickHouse, with a fast-growing community behind it.

## Why do you need a data catalog?

Although the Iceberg data and metadata files themselves live directly in object storage (like [R2 ↗](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/)), the list of tables and pointers to the current metadata need to be tracked centrally by a data catalog.

Think of a data catalog as a library's index system. While books (your data) are physically distributed across shelves (object storage), the index provides a single source of truth about what books exist, their locations, and their latest editions. Without this index, readers (query engines) would waste time searching for books, might access outdated versions, or could accidentally shelve new books in ways that make them unfindable.

Similarly, data catalogs ensure consistent, coordinated access, which allows multiple query engines to safely read from and write to the same tables without conflicts or data corruption.

## 7\. Query your data using R2 SQL

Set up your environment to use R2 SQL:

Terminal window

```

export WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN=YOUR_API_TOKEN


```

Or create a `.env` file with:

```

WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN=YOUR_API_TOKEN

Where `YOUR_API_TOKEN` is the token you created in step 3\. For more information on setting environment variables, refer to [Wrangler system environment variables](/workers/wrangler/system-environment-variables/).

Query your data:

Terminal window

```

npx wrangler r2 sql query "YOUR_WAREHOUSE_NAME" "

SELECT

    user_id,

    event_type,

    product_id,

    amount

FROM default.ecommerce

WHERE event_type = 'purchase'

LIMIT 10"


```

Replace `YOUR_WAREHOUSE_NAME` with the warehouse name from step 2.

You can also query this table with any engine that supports Apache Iceberg. To learn more about connecting other engines to R2 Data Catalog, refer to [Connect to Iceberg engines](/r2/data-catalog/config-examples/).

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **R2 Data Catalog** は Cloudflare がマネージドで提供する **Apache Iceberg REST カタログ**（Open Beta）
- R2 バケットに直接有効化するだけで、Iceberg REST catalog のエンドポイントが得られる
- dlt の Iceberg destination は `catalog_type: rest` をサポートしているので、**R2 Data Catalog を REST catalog として直接接続できる**
- さらに **R2 SQL** (`wrangler r2 sql query`) でクエリも可能。DuckDB、Spark、Snowflake 等からも接続できる
- カタログの管理が完全にマネージドなので、SQLite の永続化問題も REST catalog の運用コストも不要

## 構成図（R2 Data Catalog 版）

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  dlt-github Worker                       │
│  @cloudflare/sandbox (Python container)  │
│                                          │
│  dlt pipeline:                           │
│    source: dlt-hub/github                │
│    destination: iceberg (REST catalog)   │
│      → catalog_uri: R2 Data Catalog      │
│      → bucket: data-lake (R2)            │
└──────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
               │ Iceberg REST API
               ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  R2 Data Catalog (Managed Iceberg)       │
│  ├─ catalog endpoint (REST)              │
│  └─ data-lake bucket                     │
│      └─ github/                          │
│          ├─ repos       (Iceberg table)  │
│          ├─ stargazers  (Iceberg table)  │
│          ├─ issues      (Iceberg table)  │
│          └─ pull_requests (Iceberg table)│
└──────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
               │ Query
               ▼
        R2 SQL / DuckDB / Spark / Snowflake
```

自前でカタログを管理する必要がなく、`wrangler r2 bucket catalog enable data-lake` だけで有効化できます。dlt の `catalog_type: rest` と完璧にマッチします。

### Configure GitHub API Source Pipeline in Python

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/pipelines/rest_api/load-data-with-python-from-rest_api-to-cosmosdb

Defines a `dlt` source for the GitHub API. It configures the API client, resource defaults, and specific resources like 'issues' and 'issue_comments'. Supports incremental loading using the 'since' parameter and resolves nested resource parameters.

```python
from typing import Any

import dlt
from rest_api import (
    RESTAPIConfig,
    check_connection,
    rest_api_source,
    rest_api_resources,
)


@dlt.source
def github_source(github_token: str = dlt.secrets.value) -> Any:
    # Create a REST API configuration for the GitHub API
    # Use RESTAPIConfig to get autocompletion and type checking
    config: RESTAPIConfig = {
        "client": {
            "base_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/dlt-hub/dlt/",
            "auth": {
                "type": "bearer",
                "token": github_token,
            },
        },
        # The default configuration for all resources and their endpoints
        "resource_defaults": {
            "primary_key": "id",
            "write_disposition": "merge",
            "endpoint": {
                "params": {
                    "per_page": 100,
                },
            },
        },
        "resources": [
            # This is a simple resource definition,
            # that uses the endpoint path as a resource name:
            # "pulls",
            # Alternatively, you can define the endpoint as a dictionary
            # {
            #     "name": "pulls", # <- Name of the resource
            #     "endpoint": "pulls", # <- This is the endpoint path
            # }
            # Or use a more detailed configuration:
            {
                "name": "issues",
                "endpoint": {
                    "path": "issues",
                    # Query parameters for the endpoint
                    "params": {
                        "sort": "updated",
                        "direction": "desc",
                        "state": "open",
                        # Define `since` as a special parameter
                        # to incrementally load data from the API.
                        # This works by getting the updated_at value
                        # from the previous response data and using this value
                        # for the `since` query parameter in the next request.
                        "since": {
                            "type": "incremental",
                            "cursor_path": "updated_at",
                            "initial_value": "2024-01-25T11:21:28Z",
                        },
                    },
                },
            },
            # The following is an example of a resource that uses
            # a parent resource (`issues`) to get the `issue_number`
            # and include it in the endpoint path:
            {
                "name": "issue_comments",
                "endpoint": {
                    # The placeholder {issue_number} will be resolved
                    # from the parent resource
                    "path": "issues/{issue_number}/comments",
                    "params": {
                        # The value of `issue_number` will be taken
                        # from the `number` field in the `issues` resource
                        "issue_number": {
                            "type": "resolve",
                            "resource": "issues",
                            "field": "number",
                        }
                    },
                },
                # Include data from `id` field of the parent resource
                # in the child data. The field name in the child data
                # will be called `_issues_id` (_{resource_name}_{field_name})
                "include_from_parent": ["id"],
            },
        ],
    }

    yield from rest_api_resources(config)

```

--------------------------------

### dlt GitHub API Source Configuration

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/pipelines/rest_api/load-data-with-python-from-rest_api-to-alloydb

Configures a dlt source to fetch data from the GitHub API. It uses `RESTAPIConfig` for defining the API client, authentication (bearer token), resource defaults (primary key, write disposition), and specific resources like 'issues' and 'issue_comments'. It supports incremental loading using 'since' and resolves nested resource parameters like 'issue_number'.

```python
from typing import Any

import dlt
from rest_api import (
    RESTAPIConfig,
    check_connection,
    rest_api_source,
    rest_api_resources,
)


@dlt.source
def github_source(github_token: str = dlt.secrets.value) -> Any:
    # Create a REST API configuration for the GitHub API
    # Use RESTAPIConfig to get autocompletion and type checking
    config: RESTAPIConfig = {
        "client": {
            "base_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/dlt-hub/dlt/",
            "auth": {
                "type": "bearer",
                "token": github_token,
            },
        },
        # The default configuration for all resources and their endpoints
        "resource_defaults": {
            "primary_key": "id",
            "write_disposition": "merge",
            "endpoint": {
                "params": {
                    "per_page": 100,
                },
            },
        },
        "resources": [
            # This is a simple resource definition,
            # that uses the endpoint path as a resource name:
            # "pulls",
            # Alternatively, you can define the endpoint as a dictionary
            # {
            #     "name": "pulls", # <- Name of the resource
            #     "endpoint": "pulls",  # <- This is the endpoint path
            # }
            # Or use a more detailed configuration:
            {
                "name": "issues",
                "endpoint": {
                    "path": "issues",
                    # Query parameters for the endpoint
                    "params": {
                        "sort": "updated",
                        "direction": "desc",
                        "state": "open",
                        # Define `since` as a special parameter
                        # to incrementally load data from the API.
                        # This works by getting the updated_at value
                        # from the previous response data and using this value
                        # for the `since` query parameter in the next request.
                        "since": {
                            "type": "incremental",
                            "cursor_path": "updated_at",
                            "initial_value": "2024-01-25T11:21:28Z",
                        },
                    },
                },
            },
            # The following is an example of a resource that uses
            # a parent resource (`issues`) to get the `issue_number`
            # and include it in the endpoint path:
            {
                "name": "issue_comments",
                "endpoint": {
                    # The placeholder {issue_number} will be resolved
                    # from the parent resource
                    "path": "issues/{issue_number}/comments",
                    "params": {
                        # The value of `issue_number` will be taken
                        # from the `number` field in the `issues` resource
                        "issue_number": {
                            "type": "resolve",
                            "resource": "issues",
                            "field": "number",
                        }
                    },
                },
                # Include data from `id` field of the parent resource
                # in the child data. The field name in the child data
                # will be called `_issues_id` (_{resource_name}_{field_name})
                "include_from_parent": ["id"],
            },
        ],
    }

    yield from rest_api_resources(config)

```

--------------------------------

### Fetch GitHub Issues and Reactions with dlt.source

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/dlt-ecosystem/verified-sources/github

This Python function utilizes GraphQL to retrieve DltResource objects, specifically issues and pull requests from a GitHub repository, along with their associated reactions and comments. It requires repository owner, name, and an optional access token. The function defines resources for 'issues' with 'replace' write disposition.

```python
@dlt.source  
def github_reactions(
    owner: str,  
    name: str,  
    access_token: str = dlt.secrets.value,
    items_per_page: int = 100,
    max_items: int = None,
    max_item_age_seconds: float = None,
) -> Sequence[DltResource]:  
  
   return dlt.resource(
      _get_reactions_data(
         "issues",  
         owner,  
         name,  
         access_token,  
         items_per_page,  
         max_items,  
         max_item_age_seconds,
      ),
      name="issues",
      write_disposition="replace",
   )

```

--------------------------------

### Load GitHub Data Using Secrets Management (Python)

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/tutorial/intro

Defines a DLT source that fetches GitHub data and injects the access token using `dlt.secrets.value`. This method avoids hardcoding sensitive credentials by loading them from environment variables or a `secrets.toml` file. The source yields resources for issues, comments, and traffic clones.

```python
@dlt.source
def github_source_with_token_from_secrets(
    access_token: str = dlt.secrets.value,
):
    for endpoint in ["issues", "comments", "traffic/clones"]:
        params = {"per_page": 100}
        yield dlt.resource(
            fetch_github_data_with_token(endpoint, params, access_token),
            name=endpoint,
            write_disposition="merge",
            primary_key="id",
        )

pipeline = dlt.pipeline(
    pipeline_name="github_with_source_secrets",
    destination="duckdb",
    dataset_name="github_data",
)
load_info = pipeline.run(github_source_with_token_from_secrets())

```

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/devel/dlt-ecosystem/verified-sources/github

github_reactions| Retrieves all issues, pull requests, comments, and reactions associated with them  
github_repo_events| Gets all the repo events associated with the repository
```

## Authenticate your Iceberg engine

To connect your Iceberg engine to R2 Data Catalog, you must provide a Cloudflare API token with **both** R2 Data Catalog permissions and R2 storage permissions. Iceberg engines interact with R2 Data Catalog to perform table operations. The catalog also provides engines with SigV4 credentials, which are required to access the underlying data files stored in R2.

### Create API token in the dashboard

Create an [R2 API token](/r2/api/tokens/#permissions) with **Admin Read & Write** or **Admin Read only** permissions. These permissions include both:

* Access to R2 Data Catalog (read-only or read/write, depending on chosen permission)
* Access to R2 storage (read-only or read/write, depending on chosen permission)

Providing the resulting token value to your Iceberg engine gives it the ability to manage catalog metadata and handle data operations (reads or writes to R2).

### Create API token via API

To create an API token programmatically for use with R2 Data Catalog, you'll need to specify both R2 Data Catalog and R2 storage permission groups in your [Access Policy](/r2/api/tokens/#access-policy).

#### Example Access Policy

```

[

  {

    "id": "f267e341f3dd4697bd3b9f71dd96247f",

    "effect": "allow",

    "resources": {

      "com.cloudflare.edge.r2.bucket.4793d734c0b8e484dfc37ec392b5fa8a_default_my-bucket": "*",

      "com.cloudflare.edge.r2.bucket.4793d734c0b8e484dfc37ec392b5fa8a_eu_my-eu-bucket": "*"

    },

    "permission_groups": [

      {

        "id": "d229766a2f7f4d299f20eaa8c9b1fde9",

        "name": "Workers R2 Data Catalog Write"

      },

      {

        "id": "2efd5506f9c8494dacb1fa10a3e7d5b6",

        "name": "Workers R2 Storage Bucket Item Write"

      }

    ]

  }

]


```

To learn more about how to create API tokens for R2 Data Catalog using the API, including required permission groups a



# Disable compaction for a specific table

npx wrangler r2 bucket catalog compaction disable <BUCKET_NAME> <NAMESPACE> <TABLE>


```

## Enable snapshot expiration

Snapshot expiration automatically removes old table snapshots to reduce metadata bloat and storage costs. For more information about snapshot expiration and why it is valuable, refer to [Table maintenance](/r2/data-catalog/table-maintenance/).

Note

Snapshot expiration commands are available as of Wrangler version 4.56.0.

To enable snapshot expiration on your catalog, run the [r2 bucket catalog snapshot-expiration enable command](/workers/wrangler/commands/#r2-bucket-catalog-snapshot-expiration-enable):

Terminal window

```

# Enable catalog-level snapshot expiration (all tables)

npx wrangler r2 bucket catalog snapshot-expiration enable <BUCKET_NAME> \

  --token <API_TOKEN> \

  --older-than-days 7 \

  --retain-last 10


# Enable snapshot expiration for a specific table

npx wrangler r2 bucket catalog snapshot-expiration enable <BUCKET_NAME> <NAMESPACE> <TABLE> \

  --older-than-days 2 \

  --retain-last 5


```

## Disable snapshot expiration

Disabling snapshot expiration prevents the process from running for all tables (catalog level) or a specific table (table level). You can re-enable snapshot expiration at any time.

Terminal window

```

# Disable catalog-level snapshot expiration (all tables)

npx wrangler r2 bucket catalog snapshot-expiration disable <BUCKET_NAME>


# Disable snapshot expiration for a specific table

npx wrangler r2 bucket catalog snapshot-expiration disable <BUCKET_NAME> <NAMESPACE> <TABLE>


```

# PyIceberg

**Last reviewed:**  10 months ago 

Below is an example of using [PyIceberg ↗](https://py.iceberg.apache.org/) to connect to R2 Data Catalog.

## Prerequisites

* Sign up for a [Cloudflare account ↗](https://dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up/workers-and-pages).
* [Create an R2 bucket](/r2/buckets/create-buckets/) and [enable the data catalog](/r2/data-catalog/manage-catalogs/#enable-r2-data-catalog-on-a-bucket).
* [Create an R2 API token](/r2/api/tokens/) with both [R2 and data catalog permissions](/r2/api/tokens/#permissions).
* Install the [PyIceberg ↗](https://py.iceberg.apache.org/#installation) and [PyArrow ↗](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/install.html) libraries.

## Example usage

Python

```

import pyarrow as pa

from pyiceberg.catalog.rest import RestCatalog

from pyiceberg.exceptions import NamespaceAlreadyExistsError


# Define catalog connection details (replace variables)

WAREHOUSE = "<WAREHOUSE>"

TOKEN = "<TOKEN>"

CATALOG_URI = "<CATALOG_URI>"


# Connect to R2 Data Catalog

catalog = RestCatalog(

    name="my_catalog",

    warehouse=WAREHOUSE,

    uri=CATALOG_URI,

    token=TOKEN,

)


# Create default namespace

catalog.create_namespace("default")


# Create simple PyArrow table

df = pa.table({

    "id": [1, 2, 3],

    "name": ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"],

})


# Create an Iceberg table

test_table = ("default", "my_table")

table = catalog.create_table(

    test_table,

    schema=df.schema,

)


```

### Access Policy

An Access Policy specifies what resources the token can access and the permissions it has.

#### Resources

There are two relevant resource types for R2: `Account` and `Bucket`. For more information on the Account resource type, refer to [Account](/fundamentals/api/how-to/create-via-api/#account).

##### Bucket

Include a set of R2 buckets or all buckets in an account.

A specific bucket is represented as:

```

"com.cloudflare.edge.r2.bucket.<ACCOUNT_ID>_<JURISDICTION>_<BUCKET_NAME>": "*"

* `ACCOUNT_ID`: Refer to [Find zone and account IDs](/fundamentals/account/find-account-and-zone-ids/#find-account-id-workers-and-pages).
* `JURISDICTION`: The [jurisdiction](/r2/reference/data-location/#available-jurisdictions) where the R2 bucket lives. For buckets not created in a specific jurisdiction this value will be `default`.

# Authentication

You can generate an API token to serve as the Access Key for usage with existing S3-compatible SDKs or XML APIs.

Note

This page contains instructions on generating API tokens _specifically_ for R2\. Note that this is different from generating API tokens for other services, as documented in [Create API token](/fundamentals/api/get-started/create-token/).

You must purchase R2 before you can generate an API token.

To create an API token:

1. In the Cloudflare dashboard, go to the **R2 object storage** page.  
[ Go to **Overview** ](https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/r2/overview)
2. Select **Manage R2 API tokens**.
3. Choose to create either:  
   * **Create Account API token** \- These tokens are tied to the Cloudflare account itself and can be used by any authorized system or user. Only users with the Super Administrator role can view or create them. These tokens remain valid until manually revoked.  
   * **Create User API token** \- These tokens are tied to your individual Cloudflare user. They inherit your personal permissions and become inactive if your user is removed from the account.
4. Under **Permissions**, choose a permission types for your token. Refer to [Permissions](#permissions) for information about each option.
5. (Optional) If you select the **Object Read and Write** or **Object Read** permissions, you can scope your token to a set of buckets.
6. Select **Create Account API token** or **Create User API token**.

> AGENT

次にパイプライン本体を作ります。

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- dlt の verified GitHub source `github_reactions` は GraphQL API で issues/PRs + reactions/comments を取得
- `github_repo_events` は REST API でリポジトリイベントを取得
- 全 public repos を対象にするため、まず GitHub REST API で repos 一覧を取り、各 repo に対して source を実行する
- dlt の `pipeline.run()` は incremental loading をサポートしているので、2回目以降は差分だけ取得される
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

> TOOL

tool_use Write
id: toolu_01WeD8CxuK8vFknNe8SM2bMn
```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/pipelines/github/pipeline.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"dlt pipeline: GitHub → R2 Iceberg (via R2 Data Catalog)\n\nLoads issues, pull requests, comments, and reactions from all public repos\nof a GitHub user into Iceberg tables on R2.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\n\nimport dlt\nfrom dlt.sources.github import github_reactions, github_repo_events\n\nGITHUB_OWNER = os.environ.get(\"GITHUB_OWNER\", \"ta93abe\")\n\n\ndef get_public_repos(owner: str, token: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Fetch all public repository names for a GitHub user.\"\"\"\n    import requests\n\n    repos: list[str] = []\n    page = 1\n    while True:\n        resp = requests.get(\n            f\"https://api.github.com/users/{owner}/repos\",\n            headers={\n                \"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {token}\",\n                \"Accept\": \"application/vnd.github+json\",\n            },\n            params={\"type\": \"public\", \"per_page\": 100, \"page\": page},\n        )\n        resp.raise_for_status()\n        data = resp.json()\n        if not data:\n            break\n        repos.extend(r[\"name\"] for r in data if not r.get(\"fork\"))\n        page += 1\n    return repos\n\n\ndef run_pipeline() -> None:\n    github_token = os.environ.get(\"SOURCES__GITHUB_TOKEN\") or dlt.secrets.value\n\n    pipeline = dlt.pipeline(\n        pipeline_name=\"github_to_iceberg\",\n        destination=\"iceberg\",\n        dataset_name=\"github\",\n    )\n\n    repos = get_public_repos(GITHUB_OWNER, github_token)\n    print(f\"Found {len(repos)} public repos for {GITHUB_OWNER}\")\n\n    for repo_name in repos:\n        print(f\"\\n--- Loading {GITHUB_OWNER}/{repo_name} ---\")\n\n        # Load issues, PRs, comments, reactions\n        try:\n            reactions_source = github_reactions(\n                owner=GITHUB_OWNER,\n                name=repo_name,\n                access_token=github_token,\n                items_per_page=100,\n            )\n            load_info = pipeline.run(reactions_source)\n            print(f\"  reactions: {load_info}\")\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  reactions failed: {e}\")\n\n        # Load repo events\n        try:\n            events_source = github_repo_events(\n                owner=GITHUB_OWNER,\n                name=repo_name,\n                access_token=github_token,\n            )\n            load_info = pipeline.run(events_source)\n            print(f\"  events: {load_info}\")\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  events failed: {e}\")\n\n    print(\"\\nPipeline complete!\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    run_pipeline()\n"
}
```

GitHub トークン新しく作る

> AGENT

GitHub で Personal Access Token (Fine-grained) を作成してください。

**手順:**
1. GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → **Fine-grained tokens**
2. **Generate new token**
3. 設定:
   - Token name: `dlt-github-pipeline`
   - Expiration: 任意（90日など）
   - Resource owner: `ta93abe`
   - Repository access: **All repositories**（public repos のデータを読むため）
   - Permissions:
     - **Issues**: Read-only
     - **Pull requests**: Read-only
     - **Metadata**: Read-only（デフォルトで付与）

4. **Generate token** → トークンをコピー

### Initialize GitHub dlt Pipeline

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/devel/dlt-ecosystem/verified-sources/github

Initializes a dlt data pipeline with GitHub as the source and a specified destination (e.g., duckdb). This command creates the necessary files and configuration for the pipeline. It requires the dlt CLI to be installed.

```bash
dlt init github duckdb
```

--------------------------------

### Deploy dlt Source from a Custom Git Repository

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/devel/walkthroughs/add-a-verified-source

Example of using `dlt init` to deploy a verified source from a forked or custom Git repository. Replace `dlt-hub` with your fork name and provide the correct repository URL.

```bash
dlt init pipedrive bigquery --location "https://github.com/dlt-hub/verified-sources"
```

--------------------------------

### Initialize GitHub to AlloyDB dlt Pipeline

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/pipelines/github/load-data-with-python-from-github-to-alloydb

Creates a new project directory, initializes a dlt pipeline for GitHub source and PostgreSQL destination, and installs required dependencies. This sets up the basic structure for your data pipeline.

```bash
# create a new directory  
mkdir github_pipeline  
cd github_pipeline  
# initialize a new pipeline with your source and destination  
dlt init github postgres  
# install the required dependencies  
pip install -r requirements.txt  

```

--------------------------------

### Initialize dlt Pipeline for GitHub to Filesystem

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/pipelines/github/load-data-with-python-from-github-to-filesystem-local

Initializes a new dlt pipeline project for loading data from GitHub to the local filesystem. This involves creating a project directory, running the `dlt init` command, and installing generated dependencies.

```bash
# create a new directory  
mkdir github_pipeline  
cd github_pipeline  
# initialize a new pipeline with your source and destination  
dlt init github filesystem  
# install the required dependencies  
pip install -r requirements.txt  

```

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/devel/dlt-ecosystem/verified-sources/github

GitHub > Setup guide​ > Initialize the verified source​: This command will initialize the pipeline example with GitHub as the source and duckdb as the destination.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/dlt/github/pipeline.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"dlt pipeline: GitHub → R2 Iceberg (via R2 Data Catalog)\n\nLoads issues, pull requests, comments, reactions, events, and stargazers\nfrom all public repos of a GitHub user into Iceberg tables on R2.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport dlt\nimport requests\n\nfrom github import github_reactions, github_repo_events, github_stargazers\n\nGITHUB_OWNER = \"ta93abe\"\n\n\ndef get_public_repos(owner: str, token: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Fetch all non-fork public repository names for a GitHub user.\"\"\"\n    repos: list[str] = []\n    page = 1\n    while True:\n        resp = requests.get(\n            f\"https://api.github.com/users/{owner}/repos\",\n            headers={\n                \"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {token}\",\n                \"Accept\": \"application/vnd.github+json\",\n            },\n            params={\"type\": \"public\", \"per_page\": 100, \"page\": page},\n        )\n        resp.raise_for_status()\n        data = resp.json()\n        if not data:\n            break\n        repos.extend(r[\"name\"] for r in data if not r.get(\"fork\"))\n        page += 1\n    return repos\n\n\ndef run() -> None:\n    pipeline = dlt.pipeline(\n        pipeline_name=\"github_to_iceberg\",\n        destination=\"iceberg\",\n        dataset_name=\"github\",\n    )\n\n    token = dlt.secrets[\"sources.github.access_token\"]\n    repos = get_public_repos(GITHUB_OWNER, token)\n    print(f\"Found {len(repos)} public repos for {GITHUB_OWNER}\")\n\n    for repo_name in repos:\n        print(f\"\\n--- {GITHUB_OWNER}/{repo_name} ---\")\n\n        # Issues, PRs, comments, reactions\n        try:\n            data = github_reactions(GITHUB_OWNER, repo_name, items_per_page=100)\n            info = pipeline.run(data)\n            print(f\"  reactions: {info}\")\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  reactions failed: {e}\")\n\n        # Repo events (incremental)\n        try:\n            data = github_repo_events(GITHUB_OWNER, repo_name)\n            info = pipeline.run(data)\n            print(f\"  events: {info}\")\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  events failed: {e}\")\n\n        # Stargazers\n        try:\n            data = github_stargazers(GITHUB_OWNER, repo_name)\n            info = pipeline.run(data)\n            print(f\"  stargazers: {info}\")\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  stargazers failed: {e}\")\n\n    print(\"\\nPipeline complete!\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    run()\n"
}

```
### Install dlt with Iceberg Dependencies

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/hub/ecosystem/iceberg

Installs the dlt library with necessary dependencies for filesystem and pyiceberg integration, ensuring compatibility with dlt-plus version 0.9.1 or higher.

```shell
pip install dlt[filesystem,pyiceberg]>=1.9.1
pip install dlt-plus>=0.9.1
```

--------------------------------

### Install dlt with PyIceberg Dependency

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/devel/dlt-ecosystem/destinations/iceberg

Installs the dlt library with the necessary pyiceberg package for Iceberg table format support. Ensure Python version 3.9 or higher is used.

```bash
pip install "dlt[pyiceberg]"
```

--------------------------------

### Install dlt with Iceberg and dltHub Dependencies

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/devel/hub/ecosystem/iceberg

Installs the necessary dlt libraries for Iceberg integration and the dlthub package. Ensure you have version 1.9.1 or higher for dlt and 0.9.1 or higher for dlthub.

```bash
pip install dlt[filesystem,pyiceberg]>=1.9.1
pip install dlthub>=0.9.1
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Iceberg destination in dlt using environment variables

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/hub/ecosystem/iceberg

This snippet demonstrates how to configure an Iceberg destination using environment variables in dlt. It includes settings for catalog type, credentials, and file system. Ensure that the environment variables are set correctly before running dlt.

```bash
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__CATALOG_TYPE=rest
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__CREDENTIALS__CREDENTIAL=my_polaris_key
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__CREDENTIALS__URI=https://account.snowflakecomputing.com/polaris/api/catalog
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__CREDENTIALS__WAREHOUSE=warehouse
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__CREDENTIALS__PROPERTIES__SCOPE=PRINCIPAL_ROLE:ALL
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__FILESYSTEM__BUCKET_URL=s3://warehouse/
export DESTINATION__ICEBERG__CAPABILITIES__TABLE_LOCATION_LAYOUT={dataset_name}/{table_name}
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Iceberg destination in dlt using YAML

Source: https://dlthub.com/docs/hub/ecosystem/iceberg

This snippet demonstrates how to configure an Iceberg destination using YAML format in dlt. It includes settings for catalog type, credentials, file system, and capabilities. Sensitive information should be stored in `secrets.toml`.

```yaml
destinations:
  iceberg_lake:
    type: iceberg
    catalog_type: rest
    credentials:
      # we recommend to put sensitive configurations to secrets.toml
      credential: my_polaris_key
      uri: https://account.snowflakecomputing.com/polaris/api/catalog
      warehouse: warehouse
      properties:
        scope: PRINCIPAL_ROLE:ALL
    filesystem:
      # bucket for s3 tables - must match Lakekeeper warehouse if defined
      bucket_url: "s3://warehouse"
    capabilities:
      table_root_layout: "{dataset_name}/{table_name}"
```
```

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
dlt のオープンソース版（dlt 1.23.0）には `iceberg` は標準 destination として含まれていません。ドキュメントによると `dlt-plus` / `dlthub` パッケージ（有料）が必要です。

代替アプローチ:
1. **`filesystem` destination + `table_format="iceberg"`** — filesystem に Parquet を書き、PyIceberg で Iceberg テーブルとして管理
2. **`filesystem` destination のみ** — Parquet ファイルを R2 に書き、R2 Data Catalog に手動登録
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Iceberg destination は dlt の有料版（dlt+/dlthub）が必要です。** オープンソース版では使えません。

代わりに `filesystem` destination で R2 に Parquet を書き、**テーブルフォーマットに `iceberg` を指定する**方法があります。これはオープンソース版でサポートされています:

```python
@dlt.resource(table_format="iceberg")
def my_resource():
    ...
```

# Iceberg Destination Setup Guide

## 1. Installation

To install the Iceberg destination, run:
```bash
pip install "dlt[pyiceberg]"
pip install 'sqlalchemy>=2.0.18'
```

The documentation specifies that you need "Python version 3.9 or higher" along with these packages.

## 2. Configuration Examples

**secrets.toml** (with REST catalog):
```toml
[iceberg_catalog]
iceberg_catalog_name = "default"
iceberg_catalog_type = "rest"

[iceberg_catalog.iceberg_catalog_config]
uri = "http://localhost:8181/catalog"
type = "rest"
warehouse = "default"
```

**Alternative with S3 remote-signing:**
```toml
[iceberg_catalog.iceberg_catalog_config]
uri = "http://localhost:8181/catalog"
type = "rest"
warehouse = "default"
header.X-Iceberg-Access-Delegation = "remote-signing"
s3.access-key-id = "your-key"
s3.secret-access-key = "your-secret"
s3.region = "eu-fr-1"
```

## 3. Supported Catalog Types

The system leverages PyIceberg's `load_catalog` function and supports:
- REST catalogs
- SQL catalogs
- Single-table ephemeral catalogs
- In-memory SQLite catalogs (default fallback)

## 4. Licensing

Based on the documentation provided, dlt appears to be open-source (references to GitHub repository at github.com/dlt-hub/dlt). No mention of paid tiers is made for Iceberg functionality specifically.

## 5. REST Catalog Usage

Configuration requires specifying the REST endpoint URI and warehouse designation, as shown in the examples above. The system delegates catalog resolution to PyIceberg.

## 6. Pipeline Code Example

```python
@dlt.resource(table_format="iceberg")
def my_iceberg_resource():
    yield data_items

pipeline = dlt.pipeline("iceberg_example", destination="filesystem")
pipeline.run(my_iceberg_resource)
```
```

ドキュメントを見ると、dlt のオープンソース版でも Iceberg は使えますが、**2つの異なるアプローチ**があります:

1. **`destination="filesystem"` + `table_format="iceberg"`** — filesystem destination 上で Iceberg テーブルフォーマットを使う（PyIceberg カタログ設定が必要）
2. **`destination="iceberg"`** — 別途ドキュメントに記載があるが、これは dlt+ の可能性

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/dlt/github/pipeline.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"dlt pipeline: GitHub → R2 Iceberg (via R2 Data Catalog)\n\nLoads issues, pull requests, comments, reactions, events, and stargazers\nfrom all public repos of a GitHub user into Iceberg tables on R2.\n\nUses filesystem destination with table_format=\"iceberg\" and PyIceberg\ncatalog pointing to R2 Data Catalog (REST).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport dlt\nimport requests\n\nfrom github import github_reactions, github_repo_events, github_stargazers\n\nGITHUB_OWNER = \"ta93abe\"\n\n\ndef get_public_repos(owner: str, token: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Fetch all non-fork public repository names for a GitHub user.\"\"\"\n    repos: list[str] = []\n    page = 1\n    while True:\n        resp = requests.get(\n            f\"https://api.github.com/users/{owner}/repos\",\n            headers={\n                \"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {token}\",\n                \"Accept\": \"application/vnd.github+json\",\n            },\n            params={\"type\": \"public\", \"per_page\": 100, \"page\": page},\n        )\n        resp.raise_for_status()\n        data = resp.json()\n        if not data:\n            break\n        repos.extend(r[\"name\"] for r in data if not r.get(\"fork\"))\n        page += 1\n    return repos\n\n\ndef run() -> None:\n    pipeline = dlt.pipeline(\n        pipeline_name=\"github_to_iceberg\",\n        destination=\"filesystem\",\n        dataset_name=\"github\",\n    )\n\n    token = dlt.secrets[\"sources.github.access_token\"]\n    repos = get_public_repos(GITHUB_OWNER, token)\n    print(f\"Found {len(repos)} public repos for {GITHUB_OWNER}\")\n\n    # Start with first repo only for testing\n    for repo_name in repos[:1]:\n        print(f\"\\n--- {GITHUB_OWNER}/{repo_name} ---\")\n\n        # Issues, PRs, comments, reactions\n        try:\n            data = github_reactions(\n                GITHUB_OWNER, repo_name, items_per_page=100\n            )\n            data.issues.apply_hints(table_format=\"iceberg\")\n            data.pull_requests.apply_hints(table_format=\"iceberg\")\n            info = pipeline.run(data)\n            print(f\"  reactions: {info}\")\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  reactions failed: {e}\")\n\n        # Repo events (incremental)\n        try:\n            data = github_repo_events(GITHUB_OWNER, repo_name)\n            data.repo_events.apply_hints(table_format=\"iceberg\")\n            info = pipeline.run(data)\n            print(f\"  events: {info}\")\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  events failed: {e}\")\n\n    print(\"\\nPipeline complete!\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    run()\n"
}
```

> AGENT

進展しました！カタログ接続は成功しましたが、テーブルの保存先パスが R2 Data Catalog のストレージプロファイル（`s3://data-lake/__r2_data_catalog`）のサブパスである必要があります。

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
R2 Data Catalog はテーブルデータを `s3://data-lake/__r2_data_catalog/` 配下に格納する設計です。dlt のデフォルトレイアウト `s3://data-lake/github/...` がこの制約に合っていません。`bucket_url` を `s3://data-lake/__r2_data_catalog` に変更するか、dlt のテーブルレイアウトを調整する必要があります。
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- 現状パーティションなし（`Partition: []`）のため R2 SQL でクエリできない
- 全リポジトリのデータを1テーブルに入れるので、**リポジトリ名のカラムが必要**（現状ない）
- パーティションキーの候補: `created_at` の月単位（時系列クエリに有効）
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

2つの問題があります:

1. **リポジトリ名がカラムにない** — 全リポジトリを1テーブルに入れるとどのリポジトリのデータか分からない
2. **パーティションなし** — R2 SQL でクエリできない

dlt でこれを解決するには:
- `add_map` でリポジトリ名カラムを追加
- `apply_hints` でパーティションを設定

パーティションキーの選択肢:

| キー | メリット | デメリット |
|------|---------|-----------|
| `created_at` (月単位) | 時系列クエリに最適 | リポジトリ横断クエリに弱い |
| リポジトリ名 | リポジトリごとのフィルタに最適 | カーディナリティが高い |
| 両方 | 柔軟 | パーティション数が多くなる |

リポジトリ名を追加して、`created_at` の月単位でパーティションにするのが良さそうです。どう思いますか？

PyIceberg で直接パーティション付きテーブルを作り直す方法に切り替えます。

```json
{
  "command": "uv run python -c \"\nfrom pyiceberg.catalog.rest import RestCatalog\nfrom pyiceberg.transforms import MonthTransform\nfrom pyiceberg.partitioning import PartitionSpec, PartitionField\n\ncatalog = RestCatalog(\n    name='r2',\n    uri='https://catalog.cloudflarestorage.com/b0047256d1afc1be1df08289ee3be552/data-lake',\n    warehouse='b0047256d1afc1be1df08289ee3be552_data-lake',\n    token='REDACTED',\n)\n\n# Get current schema, then recreate with partition\nfor table_id in catalog.list_tables('github'):\n    table = catalog.load_table(table_id)\n    schema = table.schema()\n    \n    # Find created_at field\n    created_at_field = schema.find_field('created_at')\n    \n    # Drop and recreate with partition\n    print(f'Dropping {table_id}...')\n    catalog.drop_table(table_id)\n    \n    partition_spec = PartitionSpec(\n        PartitionField(\n            source_id=created_at_field.field_id,\n            field_id=1000,\n            transform=MonthTransform(),\n            name='created_at_month',\n        )\n    )\n    \n    print(f'Creating {table_id} with partition by month(created_at)...')\n    catalog.create_table(\n        table_id,\n        schema=schema,\n        partition_spec=partition_spec,\n    )\n    \n    # Verify\n    new_table = catalog.load_table(table_id)\n    print(f'  Partition spec: {new_table.spec()}')\n    print()\n\nprint('Done')\n\" 2>&1",
  "description": "Recreate tables with month partition",
  "timeout": 30000
}
```

今は1リポジトリ（`blog`）だけのテストです。全リポジトリ対応に進む前に、テーブル作成の自動化が必要です。現状は手動で PyIceberg でパーティション付きテーブルを先に作っていますが、dlt が新テーブルを作るときにパーティションなしで作ってしまう問題があります。

**選択肢:**
1. **パイプライン実行前に全テーブルをパーティション付きで事前作成** — 確実だが、スキーマ変更時に手動対応が必要
2. **dlt 実行後に PyIceberg でパーティション追加** — テーブル作成はdltに任せ、後からパーティションを設定

どちらがいいですか？

Post-load: add partitions to any unpartitioned tables\n    print(\"\\n--- Ensuring partitions ---\")\n    catalog = get_catalog()\n    ensure_partitions(catalog)\n\n    print(\"\\nPipeline complete!\")"
